facts.text: Sidney Center sits 7.2 miles east‑southeast of the village of Sidney, New York.
The town was named Sidney in 1797 after British naval officer Sir Sidney Smith, a hero of the American and French revolutionary wars.
Early settlers were drawn to the area for its location near the confluence of the Unadilla and Susquehanna rivers, which offered transportation and food.
In the 19th century, the Albany and Susquehanna Railroad and the Ontario and Western Railroad brought commerce to Sidney Center, turning it into a regional trade hub.
The Sidney Historical Association, located at 44 Grand Street, hosts a museum that showcases artifacts from Sidney’s early industries, including a French cheese factory and a silk mill.
